subject: pathology
title: Cellular Adaptations: Hypertrophy, Hyperplasia, Atrophy, and Metaplasia

steps.tx: When cells experience altered physiological demands or non-lethal pathological stresses, they achieve a new steady state through cellular adaptations. An increase in the size of individual cells resulting in overall organ enlargement is **hypertrophy**, driven by enhanced synthesis of structural proteins and functional organelles rather than cell division.
steps.say: Hypertrophy is an increase in individual cell size without cell division, expanding total organ volume.

vis.caption: Severe concentric left ventricular myocardial hypertrophy resulting from sustained pressure overload.
vis.alt: Myocardial hypertrophy demonstrating thick ventricular wall architecture

steps.tx: Hypertrophy occurs primarily in non-dividing, terminally differentiated permanent tissues that cannot undergo mitotic division. In response to chronic arterial hypertension or aortic valve stenosis, working ventricular cardiomyocytes undergo **pathological cardiac hypertrophy**, synthesizing additional sarcomeres in parallel to increase wall thickness and withstand mechanical wall tension.
steps.say: Terminally differentiated cardiac myocytes respond to hypertension with hypertrophy, adding sarcomeres in parallel.

steps.tx: In tissues capable of mitotic division, an increase in tissue mass is achieved through an increase in the actual number of cells. Termed **hyperplasia**, this adaptive proliferation is driven by growth factors and stem cell recruitment, often occurring concurrently with hypertrophy in responsive tissues like the gravid uterus during pregnancy.
steps.say: Hyperplasia increases the absolute number of cells in mitotic tissues, driven by growth factor signals.

left.title: Hypertrophy Characteristics
points: Increase in cell size and mass without increase in cell number
Occurs in permanent non-dividing tissues (skeletal muscle, cardiac myocytes)
Driven by mechanical stretch, growth factors, and vasoactive peptides
Limited by capillary perfusion and mitochondrial energy capacity

right.title: Hyperplasia Characteristics
points: Increase in absolute number of cells derived from stem cell proliferation
Occurs exclusively in labile and stable mitotic tissues (glands, liver, bone marrow)
Driven by growth factor receptor stimulation and hormonal surges
Reversible when the initiating hormonal or chemical stimulus ceases

steps.tx: Pathological hyperplasia occurs when excessive or uncoordinated hormonal stimulation or growth factor production drives abnormal cell proliferation. In aging men, excessive local accumulation of dihydrotestosterone stimulates stromal and glandular cellular proliferation within the periurethral transition zone, producing **benign prostatic hyperplasia**.
steps.say: Benign prostatic hyperplasia is an androgen-driven increase in cell number that compresses the urethra.

vis.caption: Gross cross-section of enlarged prostate displaying nodular transition-zone hyperplasia compressing the urethra.
vis.alt: Benign prostatic hyperplasia nodular expansion compressing prostatic urethra

steps.tx: Reduction in cell size and substance resulting in decreased tissue mass is atrophy. Whether caused by decreased workload, loss of innervation, diminished blood supply, or inadequate nutrition, **pathological atrophy** results from a coordinated shift where intracellular protein degradation exceeds protein synthesis.
steps.say: Atrophy is a reduction in cell size and functional mass when protein degradation outpaces synthesis.

steps.tx: A principal biochemical pathway driving muscle wasting and cell shrinkage in atrophy is the ubiquitin-proteasome system. Cytosolic and myofibrillar proteins are conjugated to multiple ubiquitin molecules by ubiquitin ligases, targeting them for rapid enzymatic destruction within the barrel-shaped **26S proteasome complex**.
steps.say: The ubiquitin-proteasome pathway flags proteins with ubiquitin for destruction inside 26S proteasomes.

left.title: Ubiquitin-Proteasome Pathway
points: Degrades cytosolic, nuclear, and myofibrillar proteins
Requires sequential cascade of E1, E2, and E3 ubiquitin ligase enzymes
Polyubiquitinated substrates threaded into 26S catalytic proteasome core
Rapidly elevated by glucocorticoids and inflammatory cytokines in cachexia

right.title: Autophagic Degradation
points: Degrades large cellular components, aggregates, and entire organelles
Sequestration into autophagosomes followed by lysosomal fusion
Digests senescent mitochondria (mitophagy) and endoplasmic reticulum
Leaves indigestible cross-linked lipid debris termed lipofuscin

steps.tx: A reversible adaptive replacement of one adult differentiated cell type by another adult cell type capable of withstanding environmental stress represents metaplasia. Arising through reprogramming of local tissue stem cells rather than direct transdifferentiation, **squamous metaplasia** replaces delicate ciliated respiratory columnar epithelium with tough stratified squamous epithelium in chronic cigarette smokers.
steps.say: Metaplasia is a reversible switch of one adult cell type for another better suited to stress.

left.title: Squamous Metaplasia (Respiratory)
points: Delicate pseudostratified ciliated columnar cells replaced by stratified squamous
Induced by chronic chemical and thermal irritation from cigarette smoke
Provides superior protective barrier against physical mechanical injury
Loss of mucus secretion and mucociliary clearance increases infection risk

right.title: Columnar Metaplasia (Barrett Oesophagus)
points: Stratified squamous epithelium of lower oesophagus replaced by columnar
Induced by chronic exposure to acidic refluxed gastric juice and bile
Contains mucin-secreting goblet cells (intestinal metaplasia)
Conveys thirty- to forty-fold elevated risk of oesophageal adenocarcinoma

steps.tx: While metaplasia confers temporary survival advantages against chronic noxious irritants, the adapted tissue loses specialized physiological functions such as ciliary clearance or mucosal secretion. If the chronic predisposing irritation persists indefinitely, metaplastic epithelium can undergo progressive genetic mutations that transform it into **dysplasia and malignant carcinoma**.
steps.say: Persistent stress causes metaplastic tissue to acquire mutations, progressing to dysplasia and cancer.
